scope.question: Can a Maxwell-equation treatment of the endogenous EM field of a parametric thalamic syncytium (HH cable neurons, gap junction coupling, cortical column controllers) produce EM manifold dynamics — standing wave patterns and folding transitions — that holographically encode 3D sensory inputs and reproduce EEG-like oscillatory signatures correlated with stimulus identity?
in_scope: Three-layer thalamo-cortical model: L1 multipole EM field from HH cable currents (Hales method), L2 gap junction topology switching, L3 phase-space meta-optimization
Cortical column controllers modulating thalamic syncytium via efferent connections
3D sensory input modeling: light field (visual) and spatial audio field (auditory)
Holographic world model encoding via standing wave interference patterns (Lehar harmonic resonance)
EEG-like oscillatory signature extraction from simulated population-level EM field dynamics
Parametric scalability: system size N tunable for computational feasibility
Efficient compute kernels for neural EM field physics
Bulk-boundary correspondence encoding as L2 phenomenon
Distributed error-correcting holographic redundancy as L3 phenomenon
out_of_scope: Full motor control loop closure (FlyWire-style) — future work
2D sensory simplification as the primary sensory model
unresolved_questions: How to bridge from Hales small-population EM field treatment to syncytium-scale collective field dynamics — new physics required
Precise gap junction switching timescales and coupling strengths in the thalamus
Which EEG signatures are most diagnostic: spindles, alpha, gamma, or cross-frequency coupling
Optimal neuron model complexity: full HH cable vs simplified compartmental for practical scalability
Decisive EEG benchmark dataset not yet selected

user_asserted_anchors: Hales endogenous EM field paper — primary method anchor for computing EM field from neural cable currents
Lehar harmonic resonance theory — primary theory anchor for holographic standing wave encoding
FlyWire/Shiu 2024 connectome simulation — scale and feasibility benchmark
known_good_baselines: EEG empirical data: thalamic spindle frequencies 7-14 Hz, cortical alpha 8-12 Hz, gamma 30-80 Hz
context_gaps: Decisive EEG benchmark dataset not yet selected — identify specific experimental paper for quantitative comparison in Phase 1
Precise gap junction coupling model for thalamic cells not specified
crucial_inputs: 3D sensory fields must be modeled as genuine spatial fields — not 2D simplifications
Virtual point sources acceptable as test stimuli inside the 3D field, but must not reduce the sensory field model itself to 2D
System must be parametrically scalable in N for feasibility testing

formulations: Maxwell equation treatment of endogenous EM field from HH cable current distributions (Hales method)
Syncytium modeled as electrically coupled network via gap junctions
Cortical columns as active boundary-condition controllers of the thalamic EM cavity
allowed_estimator_families: Full HH cable model with dendritic and axonal morphology
Simplified compartmental models as approximations with explicit validity bounds
forbidden_estimator_families: Point-neuron models that discard cable geometry
2D sensory field models as primary sensory representation
allowed_fit_families: EEG-motivated frequency analysis of simulated field dynamics
Standing wave mode decomposition of the thalamic EM field
forbidden_fit_families: Post-hoc tuning to match EEG signatures without mechanistic basis
stop_and_rethink_conditions: Simulated field dynamics show no oscillatory structure at any stimulus — rethink cell density or coupling assumptions
EEG-like signatures appear but show no correlation with stimulus identity — holographic encoding hypothesis requires revision
Computational cost makes even N~100 cells intractable — revisit EM field computation strategy before proceeding

observables.name: EEG-like oscillatory signatures
observables.definition: Power spectral density of the simulated thalamic EM field, showing peaks at biologically observed frequencies correlated with stimulus identity

observables.name: Standing wave EM field pattern
observables.definition: Spatial distribution of the EM field magnitude and phase across the thalamic syncytium, showing standing wave interference structure consistent with Lehar harmonic resonance encoding

observables.name: Holographic sensory encoding
observables.definition: Demonstration that the standing wave pattern encodes distinguishable 3D sensory inputs and can be partially recovered after simulated cell loss

claims.statement: A parametric thalamic syncytium modeled with Maxwell-equation EM field computation from HH cable currents produces EEG-like oscillatory signatures that are correlated with and distinguishable by 3D sensory input identity

The collective EM field of the syncytium forms standing wave patterns in the Lehar harmonic resonance sense that holographically encode distinguishable 3D sensory inputs with error-correcting redundancy

deliverables.description: Parametric simulation of thalamic syncytium: N HH cable neurons with gap junction coupling, cortical column controller interface, EM field computation via Maxwell equations
Power spectral density curves of simulated thalamic EM field for different 3D sensory stimuli, overlaid with empirical EEG reference frequencies
Spatial maps of the thalamic EM field showing standing wave patterns for different stimuli, plus recovery after partial cell loss

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-main
acceptance_tests.procedure: Compute PSD of simulated thalamic EM field under at least 2 distinct 3D sensory stimuli; compare peak frequencies to known EEG bands; verify PSD profiles differ between stimuli
acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Simulated PSD shows peaks within known EEG frequency bands AND profiles are statistically distinguishable across stimuli

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-holographic
acceptance_tests.procedure: Encode a test 3D sensory input as a standing wave pattern; remove 20% of syncytium cells; attempt recovery of the encoded pattern from the remaining field
acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Encoded pattern recoverable with greater than 70% fidelity after 20% cell loss, demonstrating holographic redundancy

references.locator: Hales, C. — The origins of the brain's endogenous electromagnetic field and its relationship to provision of consciousness — ResearchGate 2014
references.why_it_matters: Primary methodological anchor for computing the endogenous EM field from neural cable current distributions using Maxwell's equations — foundation of L1

references.locator: Lehar, S. — Harmonic Resonance Theory / The World in Your Head — various publications
references.why_it_matters: Primary theory anchor for holographic standing wave encoding in neural EM fields — defines what folding the manifold means and what the encoded world model structure should look like

references.locator: Shiu, P. et al. — Nature 2024 — FlyWire connectome neural simulation with MuJoCo body control
references.why_it_matters: Scale and computational feasibility anchor — demonstrates what is achievable with full connectome-scale neural simulation; target architecture to grow toward

references.locator: EEG empirical literature — thalamic spindles 7-14 Hz, cortical alpha 8-12 Hz, gamma 30-80 Hz — benchmark dataset TBD
references.why_it_matters: Smoking-gun validation target — simulated field dynamics must reproduce EEG-like frequency signatures to confirm the EM manifold hypothesis

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-main
forbidden_proxies.proxy: Neural oscillations present in the simulation but not correlated with stimulus identity
forbidden_proxies.reason: Shows the model can oscillate but not that it encodes stimulus information

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-holographic
forbidden_proxies.proxy: 2D sensory field simplification used as the primary sensory model
forbidden_proxies.reason: The hypothesis requires 3D sensory fields; 2D shortcuts invalidate the light-field and spatial-audio encoding claims

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-main
forbidden_proxies.proxy: Qualitative similarity to EEG without quantitative frequency band matching
forbidden_proxies.reason: Would look like progress while skipping the decisive benchmark comparison

weakest_anchors: Gap between Hales single-neuron EM field treatment and syncytium-scale collective field dynamics — new physics required here
Decisive EEG benchmark dataset not yet selected — benchmark reference TBD before execution
unvalidated_assumptions: The thalamic syncytium is large enough and sufficiently coupled to support standing wave modes at EEG frequencies
Maxwell-equation treatment of HH cable currents gives a good approximation of the macroscopic EM field at syncytium scale
Gap junction switching timescales are compatible with holographic encoding timescales
competing_explanations: EEG-like signatures could emerge from synaptic current dynamics alone without requiring the full EM field treatment — would undermine L1 necessity
Holographic encoding in the brain may be implemented at the synaptic weight level rather than the physical EM field level
disconfirming_observations: Simulated EM field dynamics show no oscillatory structure at any stimulus
EEG-like signatures appear but are identical across all stimuli
Computational cost makes even N~100 cells intractable with Maxwell+HH approach

open_questions: How to bridge from Hales small-population EM field treatment to syncytium-scale collective field dynamics — new physics required
Precise gap junction switching timescales and coupling strengths in the thalamus
Which EEG signatures are most diagnostic: spindles, alpha, gamma, or cross-frequency coupling
Optimal neuron model complexity: full HH cable vs simplified compartmental for practical scalability
Decisive EEG benchmark dataset not yet selected

convention_lock.fourier_convention: Physics asymmetric: f_tilde(omega) = integral f(t) exp(-i*omega*t) dt; inverse: f(t) = integral [d_omega/(2*pi)] f_tilde(omega) exp(+i*omega*t); consistent with scipy.signal and MNE-Python
convention_lock.coupling_convention: Gap junction: I_gap_i = g_j*(V_i-V_j); outward-positive from cell i; g_j in nS range 0.1-10; K = g_j/(g_j+g_m) dimensionless

custom_conventions.observable: LFP (local field potential), NOT scalp EEG; amplitude in V/m or uV; compare to LFP literature (Linden et al. 2010)
custom_conventions.unit_system: SI for EM (V/m, A, S/m); neural units (mV, ms, nS, uF/cm2, uA/cm2, um); NO CGS; conversion: 1 uV/cm = 0.1 mV/m
custom_conventions.HH_current_sign: outward_positive; I_ion = g*(V_m-E_ion); h = fraction NOT inactivated; h_inf(-65mV)=0.596; C_m dV/dt = -I_Na-I_K-I_L-I_T-I_h-I_NaP+I_ext
custom_conventions.membrane_potential_sign: V_m = V_intracellular - V_extracellular; resting = -65 mV; AP peak = +40 mV; AHP = -75 mV
custom_conventions.EM_approximation: quasi-static Poisson: ∇·(σ∇φ) = -∇·J_imp; σ=0.33 S/m; retardation ratio L/lambda ~ 3e-8 at 1kHz and 1cm; full Maxwell adds nothing at neural scales
custom_conventions.standing_wave_definition: LFP spatial eigenmode of network dynamics (NOT EM radiation mode); dominant left singular vector U[:,0] of LFP snapshot matrix; spatial period set by network architecture not EM wavelength
custom_conventions.holographic_fidelity: rho = Pearson(F_original, F_reconstructed) >= 0.70 after 20% cell loss; F = U[:,0] dominant SVD mode; compare to matched-N random distributed code baseline
custom_conventions.Kuramoto_order_parameter: R = (1/N)*|sum_k exp(i*theta_k)|; subcritical R<0.2; supercritical R>0.8; g_j^c = coupling threshold at max dR/dg_j
custom_conventions.simulation_timestep: dt <= 0.025 ms; never exceed 0.05 ms; Crank-Nicolson for cable; backward/exponential Euler for HH gates; initialize gates to steady-state at V=-65mV; 100ms settling before recording
